skill.name: ticket-workflow
skill.desc: Task tracking bound to git worktrees. Tickets are conversation outcomes that become claimable work units.
skill.overview:
Tickets represent concrete work to be done. They emerge from conversations (inbox or retro processing) and flow through directories that map to git worktrees. Each ticket is a markdown file with frontmatter; the filename becomes the branch name and worktree name.
Directory = state. File movement = state change. Worktree = isolated workspace.
skill.structure:
``` META/tickets/ todo/ # Unclaimed, ready to work in-progress/ # Claimed, has worktree review/ # Awaiting human review done/ # Merged and complete ```
Filename = slug: `feature-name.md` → branch `feature-name` → worktree `_feature-name/`
skill.frontmatter:
```yaml --- priority: high | medium | low project: myproject created_at: 2025-12-27 source: META/inbox/20251227-1030-feature-idea.md --- ```
- `priority` - High, medium, or low - `project` - Which project this belongs to - `created_at` - When the ticket was created - `source` - Optional. The inbox/retro item that spawned this ticket
skill.format:
```markdown --- priority: medium project: saddle created_at: 2025-12-27 --- # TICKET Single sentence goal.
Context paragraph explaining the work.
# CODE SNIPPETS Implementation patterns (optional).
# NOTES - Constraints, dependencies, considerations - Non-actionable context
# TASKS - [ ] Phase 1: Name - [ ] Task with `file/path.rs` - [ ] Another task - [ ] Phase 2: Name - [ ] More tasks ```
Rules: - Actionable tasks only in TASKS section - File paths in backticks - Action verbs (Add, Update, Remove, Fix) - Non-actionable info goes in NOTES

lifecycle.create: Write to `todo/{slug}.md`, get approval before claiming.
lifecycle.claim: ```bash mv META/tickets/todo/{slug}.md META/tickets/in-progress/ cd main && git worktree add ../_{slug} -b {slug} cd ../_{slug} && git submodule update --init --recursive ```
lifecycle.work: Execute tasks in worktree. Mark complete as you go. Run tests.
lifecycle.submit: ```bash mv META/tickets/in-progress/{slug}.md META/tickets/review/ ``` Then STOP. Wait for human review.
lifecycle.review: Audit tasks, run tests, inspect diff. If changes needed, add Review Addendum.
lifecycle.merge: On human approval: ```bash cd _{slug} && git rebase -i main # squash commits cd ../main && git merge {slug} --ff-only rm -rf ../_{slug} && git worktree prune git branch -d {slug} mv ../META/tickets/review/{slug}.md ../META/tickets/done/ ```

skill.flow: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Todo: Create ticket Todo --> InProgress: Claim (creates worktree) InProgress --> Review: Submit Review --> InProgress: Changes requested Review --> Done: Approved + Merge Done --> [*] ```
skill.file_movement:
**CRITICAL**: Tickets must exist in exactly ONE directory at a time.
Use `mv` (move), never `cp` (copy). After moving: ```bash mv META/tickets/todo/{slug}.md META/tickets/in-progress/ ls META/tickets/todo/{slug}.md # should fail: No such file ```
Duplicate tickets across stages = corrupted state.

addendums.ticket_addendum:
Scope expansion before review submission: ```markdown ---
# TICKET ADDENDUM
Reason for expansion.
- [ ] Phase N: New Work - [ ] Task ```
addendums.review_addendum:
Fixes after review feedback: ```markdown ---
# REVIEW ADDENDUM
What changed during review.
- [x] Phase N: Review Fixes - [x] Fix applied ```

skill.as_outcome:
Tickets are conversation outcomes. When processing an inbox item or reviewing a retro, a ticket may be created:
```yaml # In the inbox item's frontmatter after processing: --- status: done outcome: ticket outcome_ref: META/tickets/todo/feature-name.md --- ```
The ticket's `source` field can reference back to the originating item for traceability.
skill.multi_agent: Directory structure = implicit coordination: - `in-progress/` = claimed, don't touch - Only claim from `todo/` - One agent per ticket, one ticket per worktree
skill.commits:
Before committing, study the changes: - `git diff --stat` to see changed files - `git diff -p` to understand what changed - Look for patterns: deletions, creations, renames, refactors
Commit message format: - Title: imperative mood, clear, concise, no period - Body: 1-3 bullet points explaining what and why - Technical and direct, no fluff - NO "Generated with", NO co-author tags
skill.priority: Three levels: - **high** - Blocking other work, critical bug, urgent - **medium** - Normal feature work, standard bugs - **low** - Nice to have, tech debt, cleanup
